images.note: Later depiction: Gilbert Stuart painted this c.1785, 25 years after De Lancey's death (1760). Covers De Lancey's judge role in the Zenger trial.
images.title: James DeLancey, by Gilbert Stuart, ca. 1785

images.note: 1756 Lancaster reprint (not the 1736 first edition) of the famous trial account; title page names Zenger as 'Printer of the New-York Weekly-Journal'. Covers the trial, acquittal, and press beats.
images.source: Internet Archive (John Carter Brown Library copy)
images.title: Title page, A Brief Narrative of the Case and Trial of John Peter Zenger, 1756 reprint

images.note: Contemporary: both teapots are English-made in the 1740s. Covers the Anglicization beat ('drinking English tea').
images.title: Silver teapot, Paul de Lamerie, London, 1743-44

images.note: Contemporary 1728 map dedicated to Massachusetts governor William Burnet; covers the royal-governor salary-fight beat (Burnet, Shute).
images.source: National Gallery of Art, History of Early American Landscape Design wiki (original at Library of Congress)
images.title: A Plan of Boston in New England, William Burgis, 1728

images.alt_source: Wellcome Collection, London (Hogarth, 'The Five Orders of Periwigs', 1761)
images.note: Contemporary 1761 satirical print of English wig fashions; covers the Anglicization beat ('wearing wigs').
images.title: The Five Orders of Periwigs, William Hogarth, 1761

images.note: Contemporary: Chinese export porcelain teapot, ca. 1740. Covers the Anglicization beat ('china in the china cabinet').
images.title: Chinese export porcelain teapot and saucer, Qing dynasty, ca. 1740

images.note: Contemporary: longcase clock made in London, 1766, pre-Revolution. Covers the Anglicization beat ('English ticking clocks').
images.title: Longcase clock, Mario Gambelli, London, 1766

images.note: Later depiction: 1779 satirical print, 32 years after the 1747 Knowles impressment riot in Boston; shows a press gang seizing a man in London. Covers the impressment/riot beat.
images.title: The Liberty of the Subject [the Press Gang], attr. James Gillray, 1779

images.note: Later depiction: 1857 painting of the Georgian mansion, post-colonial. Covers the Anglicization beat ('living in English houses').
images.source: George Washington's Mount Vernon (Mount Vernon Ladies' Association)
images.title: The Old Mount Vernon, Eastman Johnson, 1857

images.note: Contemporary 1770 print (post-dates the episode's 1763 close, but the beat is explicitly forward-looking: 'new taxes and new rules, with redcoats staying put').
images.source: Boston Public Library, via Digital Commonwealth
images.title: The Bloody Massacre perpetrated in King-Street Boston, Paul Revere, 1770
